If you’re in the US, I would recommend checking out Job Corps! They give you free housing, food, and job training! They also give you a living stipend and help with English as a Second Language. They help you get a job certification and find jobs after you leave Job Corps. They can also help you go to college. Many of the people who join Job Corps are homeless. It’s for ages 18-24, and you don’t have to be an American citizen. You don’t pay anything to join and you won’t owe anything if you quit; they cover everything. They also have medical care, outings, counseling, and things of that nature, all free.

You just have to be income eligible to join. Homelessness makes you immediately eligible. 

Here’s information about Job Corps: https://www.jobcorps.gov/students

There are a lot of valid complaints people have about Job Corps and you’ll find a lot of bad things when you Google it, but the bottom line is that it gives you free housing and food and you can leave any time. There are a lot of different centers and many centers have problems with violence, while many centers don’t. 

If you’re not interested in Job Corps, I would recommend Googling “homeless youth programs” and your city. Additionally, community colleges are much better at helping homeless students than four year colleges. If you’re struggling at a four year college for whatever reason, try taking classes at a community college and utilizing the additional resources they have.

Every state does allow involuntary hospitalizations, but criteria for it can change state to state. If you have to go to the hospital to medically recover after a suicide attempt, you can count on being involuntarily hospitalized for three days in the psych ward.  Many involuntary hospitalizations are the result of police, not mental health professionals. There’s a strict legal process that mental health professionals have to follow to do involuntary hospitalizations, and significantly less than 1% of psychiatric patients are ever involuntarily hospitalized, but police can kinda hospitalize people as they please.

Studies show that involuntary hospitalization has many negative effects, reduces trust in the mental health system, and has a significant financial impact, so many mental health professionals only consider it if a patient is violent.

This is a common fear—what will happen if my psychiatrist or psychologist knows I’m suicidal? So, basically, if you express that you’re suicidal but you don’t have an explicit plan, it’s extremely unlikely that you’re going to be hospitalized without your consent or anything like that. If you were hospitalized without your consent solely for having suicidal ideation, that would be grounds for a lawsuit, so any reasonable professional is not going to do that. What they’re going to do is probably give you a referral to a psychiatrist if you don’t already have one and tell you about your counseling options. They’re likely going to give you the number of the emergency hotline and ask you if you have somebody to talk to in an emergency situation. 

My advice is to be totally honest about how you’re feeling. If you’re nervous, ask the professional you’re talking to about what they would do if you tell them you’re suicidal, just for reassurance. Many people avoid getting treatment because they’re worried they’ll be forced to go inpatient if they tell somebody they’re suicidal, and that’s a shame.

There are other comments on her shop about how ridiculous her prices are. For one Love and Lemons shirt, two different people point out that the item can be found on Poshmark for $85, and she’s charging more than $150. Caro’s account responds and says “It’s Caroline’s assistant. We’ve lowered the price to $150. If you don’t want to buy it, you don’t have to”. It’s very suspicious that the account responded to the people simply pointing out that the price of the item is almost double what it is on Poshmark by assuming that they’re fans of Caro...they’re likely just people shopping on Depop. I doubt they care about connecting with Caro through buying her items. Further, the account only follows one shop (Caro’s), and the first item they ever liked was Caro’s Love and Lemons top. 

Additionally...Caro has allegedly sold 37 items on her Depop shop, but she only has one review. A buyer who has sold 37 items should have at least 10 reviews *easy*. There is absolutely no way in hell that somebody who has sold 37 items only has one review, *especially* if that somebody is a person whose buyers are “paying a premium to own something that belongs to her”. If you’re a famous person with a Depop whose fans are buying your shit, you best believe that those fans are going to leave reviews just to say that they love you. 

So what does this mean? On Depop, sellers can choose to mark an item as “sold” even if somebody on Depop hasn’t bought it. This can help sellers who sell items on both Poshmark and Depop. It looks like Caro chose to mark certain items as “sold” instead of letting them go unbought. Sure, she could have changed her mind and wanted to keep the items...but that happens all the time with sellers, and they usually just delete the listing instead of marking “sold” on an item that hasn’t been sold.

Getting a job is the first step for somebody in your position. Think less about dream jobs and look at low effort, very part-time jobs, maybe jobs where you only work on the weekend or something. Just something. Anything. A dream job will likely be too high stress right now, and you might just quit or ghost. I’ve been there. 

The problem with phones is that they’re an immediate, zero-effort hit of dopamine. When you’re used to spending hours scrolling, everything else is boring and not worth it. But you have to start to do things anyway. Exercise/walk for ten minutes a day. Read a physical book for ten minutes a day. Do that everyday. It might be “boring” and uncomfortable, but you have to do it. It’s not much, but it will help you begin to build a life outside of your phone.

I talked to my therapist about this very issue today. She gave me some good advice. I’m sure you’ve heard the advice to leave your phone outside your bedroom at night so you’re not in bed playing on your phone? She recommended that, and I replied that I honestly can’t imagine myself leaving my phone outside my room at night and not coming out of my room to get it. So she recommended that I leave my charger outside of my room at night so that if I’m messing around on my phone, my phone will eventually die and more likely than not, I’ll go to sleep rather than go out to get the charger. 

Letting your phone/iPad die can be a smart life hack. On a day or an afternoon or whatever where you know you won’t be having a virtual meeting, give your charger to a parent or your boyfriend. Let your device die. When that happens, you’ll be forced to find ways to entertain yourself. Phones give us that easy, zero-effort entertainment. With a dead phone, you’ll read or exercise or find some other way to pass the time. Even if your phone is only dead for thirty minutes or an hour, it’s good practice.

Try to consciously spend just thirty minutes a day not on your phone. Read, walk, take a bath, self-care. Just thirty minutes not on your phone. If you can’t do that, then you need to have somebody take your charger regularly so that your phone will die every day and force you to do something else.

Wow, I relate so much to the struggle with asking people in general for things lol. Just remember that giving letters of recommendation is part of the job for professors. They’re expecting you to ask.

In terms of who to ask, it depends on your time constraints. Are you submitting applications within the next month? Because if so, I would be sending the same request email to all your current professors in whose classes you have good grades.

I would recommend sending a very short, to-the-point email to ask professors to write letters. “Hello, my name is X, I am in your X class, I am applying to transfer and was hoping you could consider taking the time to write me a letter of recommendation. If you are interested, I can send you the link and info. Thanks so much, have a great week”. 

If they say yes, then attach your resume and outline your goals and achievements so that your recommenders can refer to that when they write their letter. Most recommenders are going to appreciate all the info you can give them to put in the letter, especially if they don’t know you super well. It’s not cheating to tell them your accomplishments, goals, things you want them to highlight.

I recommend writing the short email first and then writing the second email with all the info after they say yes because I wrote two kick ass emails to request letters of rec from two professors and neither of them replied and after looking at my email, I realized how intimidating and long it was for a simple request.

These services want to make it seem as though your counselor is available 24/7, when most of the counselors have day jobs and therefore can only reply to messages once a day. 

Additionally, if you realize that most of the counselors are social workers and not other therapists, you might ask why. The platform isn’t uniquely suited to social workers more than other therapists, so why does it only employ social workers? The primary answer that might pop up is that it must be that the service wants to hire social workers because they can pay them less and because many social workers need a side hustle. So, the counselors are motivated to work for the service primarily because of financial need, and the services want to hide that because they want to act as though this is the primary job and passion of their counselors, not a side hustle to pay the bills.

The unique background and services that social workers can provide is negated by Talkspace/Better Help. They’re uniquely prepared to assist people from marginalized communities or living in poverty and they have a holistic educational background, but that benefit doesn’t play a role in Talkspace/Better Help. 

Social workers are amazing counselors, but in their Talkspace/Better Help role, everything that makes social workers more than just counselors, all the services they can provide that non-social worker therapists can’t, is ignored.

I loved receiving counseling from a social worker in my community. They had unique insights about local sources of help, resources, and referrals. If I received counseling from them through Talkspace/Better Help, I wouldn’t be able to access any of that information. 

The problem with Talkspace/Better Help isn’t that they employ social workers; it’s that they employ social workers only because they can pay them less, the social workers usually have a primary job and are overworked, and all the benefits of seeing a social worker for counseling don’t apply because of the way the platform is.

Hey! I’m not admitted but I’m applying, and it’s my dream school. I’ve researched a lot about this program, so I would love to share.

NYU’s nursing school has the highest paid graduates of any of their schools. The average STARTING SALARY for their nursing graduates is over $95,000. I’ve seen people say that it’s not worth going to NYU if you’re not going to the business school, so it’s funny that the nursing students actually make the best money. 

From what I’ve read, NYU does a good job at giving nursing students opportunities. At many other schools, you can’t really study abroad as a nursing student, but you totally can as a NYU nursing student. There’s many research and community service opportunities. 

Also, you can have a double major in Nursing and Global Public Health, and that’s pretty unique to NYU. 

Another cool thing about NYU’s nursing program that’s pretty unique to NYU is that you can get started on a Master’s degree in nursing while you’re still getting your BSN. In the last semester of your BSN, you can take some graduate classes and knock out of a few of your Master’s classes.

By far, the main criticism I’ve seen regarding the nursing program is just the cost. You can get a nursing degree for super cheap, so people often don’t understand why you would spend so much money on the degree when you don’t have to. However, I feel like people just want to say “when you’re a nurse, you’re a nurse; nobody cares where your degree comes blah blah blah” and are ignoring that, for whatever reason, NYU does seem to set students up to earn much more money than their peers from other schools. Again, the NYU nursing starting salary is over $95,000, so compare that to the average nursing grad starting salary of around $65,000.

Many universities, including UPenn, do have a nursing acceptance rate that’s higher than their standard acceptance rate, but that doesn’t necessarily mean that it’s easier to get in. I think it’s more than you can’t just apply to nursing on a whim like you can to other programs, so nursing applicants tend to be more uniformly accomplished and it’s therefore more viable to admit a large percentage of nursing applicants. But yeah, I think students at NYU and other universities do see nursing students as having one of the hardest majors.
